column1: # docs/claims.tsv — the behaviour-claim registry.
# Every line inside a <!-- rabadon:claims-begin --> block in docs/commands.md,
# docs/faq.md or docs/uninstall.md that matches the claim grammar
# (does NOT | will report | reports the | never | always | is not) must have a
# row here, and every row here must still be such a line. native/docs_truth_test.sh
# enforces both directions and RUNS the check named in column 4 against the real
# native/rabadon-gate, comparing its output to column 5.
# Why: on 2026-08-26 all three of those pages described a gate that had not
# existed since F1d — three silencers instead of six, and `rm ~/.rabadon/silent`
# as the lift for a silencer that command does not lift. The suite was green
# because nothing held prose to the binary. This file is that hold.
# Columns, tab separated:
#   1 file    the doc the line lives in
#   2 key     cksum of the trimmed line (POSIX cksum, so no python/node needed).
#             Rewording or rewrapping the line changes the key on purpose: the
#             sentence has to be re-measured, not silently inherited.
#   3 text    the line, verbatim, so a reviewer sees what was measured
#   4 check   a check name native/docs_truth_test.sh can execute. An unknown
#             name answers UNKNOWN-CHECK and can match no expectation.
#   5 expect  what that check printed on 2026-08-26, on the shipped binary
# A row whose line QUOTES a sentence that was measured FALSE is registered the
# same way: the check is the measurement that refutes it, and column 5 is that
# measurement's answer. The machine proves the measurement still holds and that
# no claim line escaped this file; a human still reads the sentence.
